column3: Close to the Hebrew; NASB follows the shorter Hebrew text, without the longer Septuagint wording. “Ruler” is rendered as “a ruler over His inheritance.”
“Abandoned the matter of the she-asses” is rendered “ceased to be concerned about the donkeys.”
“The great tree of Tabor” is rendered “the oak of Tabor,” and “skin of wine” as “jug of wine.”
“Ask you about welfare” is rendered “greet you.”
“Gibeah of God” is rendered “the hill of God,” and “garrisons” as “garrison.”
“Will rush on you” is rendered “will come upon you mightily.”
“What your hand finds” is rendered “what the occasion requires.”
Close to the Hebrew; “may you wait” is rendered “You shall wait.”
“Turned his shoulder” is rendered “turned his back,” and “changed for him another heart” as “changed his heart.”
“Gibeah” is rendered “the hill,” and “rushed on him” as “came upon him mightily.”
“From yesterday three days ago” is rendered “previously.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“We saw that not” is rendered “they could not be found.”

Close to the Hebrew; “plainly” renders the emphatic Hebrew verb.
Close to the Hebrew.
“From the hand of Egypt” is rendered “the Egyptians,” and the second “hand” as “power.”
The Hebrew reads “for a king you will appoint”; NASB has “No, but set a king,” as in many manuscripts. “Families” is rendered “clans.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB keeps the clan as “the Matrite family.”
“Into the baggage” is rendered “by the baggage.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“May the king live” is rendered “Long live the king!”
“The right(s) of the kingship” is rendered “the ordinances of the kingdom.”
“The army” (Hebrew הַחַיִל) is rendered “the valiant men.”
“He was like one who kept silent” is rendered “he kept silent.”
